title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Florin quenching distinguishes rapid single-event execution from repeated-cycle improvement
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Sloane73 Q3 separately asks for sudden quenching so the receiving water is not wasted, fifty or more repetitions because oftener is better, replacement if water wastes too much, and final pooling. Speed of one quench, count of cycles, liquid quantity loss, and asserted improvement are four distinct properties. The passage does not say rapid execution is a purity grade, and better from repetition does not specify a measured purity value. Keep the same florin across replacement liquid batches; pooling follows completed quenching. No target word or meaning is selected.

design.architecture: heat same florin -> sudden quench to limit liquid loss -> repeat fifty-plus cycles -> conditionally replace depleted liquid -> pool batches after quenching
constraints: Suddenly describes one execution event; oftener describes repeated-event frequency/count, not the same temporal modifier.
Water waste controls replacement; the text does not equate less remaining water with poorer or purer material.
The source assertion better is an unspecified comparative result, not a measured purity or quantitative concentration.
Pool all receiving liquids only after quenching; retain coin identity while allowing liquid batch replacement.

source_evidence.quote:
if ȝe be pore, ȝe schal preie a riche man þat is ȝoure freend to leene ȝou a good floreyn of florence / and anele it vpon a plate of yren as yren is anelid. and haue biside ȝou a uessel of erþe glasid, fillid ful of the beste brennynge watir þat ȝe may fynde. & caste into þe watir þe floreyn anelid. and loke þat ȝe haue a sotilte and a sleiȝþe to quenche sodeynly þe fier, þat þe watir waaste not; and be weel war þat non yren touche þe watir. but af[t]er caste into þe watir þe floreyn,

and do so .l. tymes or more, for þe oftere þe bettere it is / And if ȝe se þat þe watir waaste to myche, chaunge it þanne, and take newe, & do so ofte tymes. and whanne ȝe haue do ȝoure quenchour, putte all þe watris togidere /
